intervals.label: operating and expanding
intervals.note: Status recorded as construction to reflect the still-expanding design; see the separate commissioning interval below for concurrent data-taking.
intervals.quote: Since then, there has been an annual increase of the deployed clusters.

intervals.label: deployed clusters taking physics data (ongoing)
intervals.note: Verification fix (2026-09-17): already-deployed clusters take data continuously while the array keeps growing (same overlapping pattern used for detector:km3net-arca/orca); a bare 'construction' status alone understated this.
intervals.quote: The Baikal-GVD data collected in 2018-2022 indicate the presence of cosmic neutrino flux in high-energy cascade events consistent with observations by the IceCube neutrino telescope.

placements.quote: The first cluster of the Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope was deployed in 2016 with 288 OMs.

depth_max.quote: The lakebed reaches its plateu at a nearly constant depth of 1 366 m.

summary.plain: Clusters of light-sensing spheres hanging on strings deep in Lake Baikal, added year after year since 2016, that together form a growing telescope for neutrinos from space.
summary.technical: Modular underwater water-Cherenkov array in Lake Baikal; clusters of 8 strings x 36 OMs deployed annually since 2016; 3456 OMs on 96 strings as of the winter 2023 campaign; lakebed depth ~1366 m; already-deployed clusters have taken continuous physics data since 2018.

technology.value: Underwater water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: photomultiplier-equipped optical modules on vertical strings organised into clusters
